purpose: Telmisartan is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of heart attack and stroke. It is also used to protect your heart and blood vessels if you are at high risk for heart problems. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps your heart, kidneys, and brain stay healthier.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and squeeze, which raises your blood pressure. Telmisartan blocks the place where that chemical tries to attach, so your blood vessels stay relaxed and open. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a safer level.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication very well. Some people may notice dizziness, especially when standing up quickly, a stuffy or runny nose, back pain, upset stomach, or mild tiredness. These effects are usually mild and often go away as your body adjusts.
warnings: Do NOT take telmisartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, low blood pressure, or if you are dehydrated. Avoid taking it with potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without asking your doctor first. Let all your doctors and dentists know you take this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 40 mg taken once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may adjust your dose to anywhere between 20 mg and 80 mg per day depending on how your blood pressure responds. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember, and never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
